If you prefer we can do Option B (16:00 CET) — call it out and we'll send the invite anchored to Europe/Berlin.

Thanks!

Quick note on the GCal behavior we saw: when an invite is forwarded from an external assistant, some clients mark it as a floating event (no timezone) — GCal then interpolates based on the recipient's local zone and DST rules, which can switch the wall-clock time by an hour for people in regions where DST differs or if the original invite lacked an explicit TZ. Anchoring to a named TZ (Europe/Berlin) + including UTC in the title avoids that.
